questions.question: What is the primary advantage of using :focus-visible over :focus?
options: It displays focus outlines only when the user navigates via keyboard (Tab key), preventing focus rings on mouse clicks
It converts buttons to high-contrast monochrome
It eliminates the need for HTML labels
questions.hint: Shows focus rings only for keyboard users.
questions.explanation: :focus-visible only applies when the browser determines that focus should be visually evident (such as keyboard Tab navigation).

questions.question: Which pseudo-class styles a parent container whenever any element inside it receives focus?
questions.explanation: :focus-within matches an element if the element itself or any descendant within it matches :focus.

questions.question: How does the :has() pseudo-class revolutionize CSS selector architecture?
options: It acts as a relational parent selector, allowing parents to be styled based on their child elements
questions.explanation: :has() allows developers to style an element based on its descendant or sibling elements, acting as the long-awaited parent selector.

questions.question: What does the selector input:checked + label target?
options: The label immediately following a checked checkbox or radio button
questions.hint: Adjacent sibling combinator after a checked input.
questions.explanation: input:checked + label targets the immediate sibling label of an input that is currently checked.

questions.question: Which pseudo-class targets an element whose ID matches the current URL hash fragment (e.g. #faq-3)?
questions.explanation: The :target pseudo-class represents a unique element with an ID matching the URL's fragment identifier.
